We need to produce BPMN XML model with one pool for organisation, lanes for each actor. Actors: claim is received (maybe system?), check insurer (maybe system?), inform claimant (maybe staff?), evaluate severity (system?), send forms (maybe staff?), receive forms (maybe claimant - external?), check completeness (staff), register claim (system). For simplicity maybe use three lanes: Claim Reception (System), Claims Officer (role), Claimant (external). But claimant is outside organisation, maybe separate pool. The instruction: one pool for the organisation and one lane for each actor that performs activities. If the text names no actor, use a single lane. The claimant is external, not part of organisation, but activities: inform claimant, send forms, receive forms are interactions with claimant. Usually external party as separate pool. But spec says one pool for org. For external parties we could still create a lane representing Claimant within same pool? But that would be inaccurate. Probably better: one organization pool with lanes: Claims Intake (System?), Claims Officer (role). And claimants interaction could be modelled via message flows to external pool. But requirement: Use one pool for the organisation and one lane for each actor (a person, role, department or system) that performs activities. If the text names no actor, use a single lane. It does not forbid external pool, but we could include external pool with participant without processRef (black-box). That would be okay.

Let's design:

Pool "Organization" with lanes:
- "Reception System" (handles claim receipt)
- "Claims Officer" (checks insurance, evaluates severity, checks forms, registers claim)
- maybe "Claims Management System" is same as officer? Actually registration in system can be task by system.

We can have three lanes: "Reception System", "Claims Officer", "Claims Management System". Claimant as external pool with participant name "Claimant". Activities interacting with claimant occur via message flows.

Simplify: Use two lanes: "Claims Officer" handles most tasks; claim receipt as start event maybe "Claim received". Could be system, but not needed.

Probably easiest: one pool with single lane "Claims Process". Use tasks for all steps. No external pool.

The instruction: "When a claim is received, it is first checked whether the claimant is insured by the organization." So start event "Claim received". Task "Check insurance". Exclusive gateway "Insured?" Yes/No. No -> Task "Inform claimant of rejection". End event "Process ended (rejected)". Yes -> Task "Evaluate claim severity". Exclusive gateway "Simple claim?" Yes/No. But "Based on the outcome (simple or complex claims), relevant forms are sent to the claimant." So after evaluation, task "Send relevant forms". Then wait for forms returned (receive task?). Could be intermediate catch event "Forms returned". Then Task "Check forms for completeness". Exclusive gateway "Forms complete?" Yes/No. Yes -> Task "Register claim in Claims Management system". End event "Claims Notification process ends". No -> Task "Inform claimant to update forms". Then wait for updated forms (receive). Then loop back to "Check forms for completeness" (maybe via sequence flow).

Thus need loop.

Implement tasks names exactly: Use words from text: "Check insurance", "Inform claimant of rejection", "Evaluate claim severity", "Send relevant forms", "Check forms for completeness", "Register claim in Claims Management system", "Inform claimant to update forms". For receive forms we may use "Receive forms". The text: "Once the forms are returned" implies wait. Use intermediate catch event "Forms returned". Similarly "Upon reception of the updated forms". Use intermediate catch event "Updated forms received".

We need exclusive gateway decisions "Insured?" and "Forms complete?" and maybe after severity we don't need decision gateway, because just send forms. No need a gateway for simple/complex - same action "Send relevant forms". So can omit.

Thus model.

We need to check element naming: start event could be "1. Claim received". Task names should start with step number from description. Steps are in description but not numbered; we can assign numbers sequentially: 1 Claim received (start event), 2 Check insurance, 3 Inform claimant of rejection, 4 Evaluate claim severity, 5 Send relevant forms, 6 Receive forms, 7 Check forms for completeness, 8 Register claim..., 9 Inform claimant to update forms, 10 Receive updated forms, etc. Start event not required to start with number? spec says only plain end events and start events inside a sub-process may have no number. So start event can be without. We'll name start event just "Claim received". End events can be no number.

Tasks names must start with step number. We'll number as described.

Thus tasks: "2. Check insurance", "3. Inform claimant of rejection", "4. Evaluate claim severity", "5. Send relevant forms", "7. Check forms for completeness", "8. Register claim in Claims Management system", "9. Inform claimant to update forms". Also we have "6. Receive forms" maybe as intermediate catch event not task. However the step "Once the forms are returned, they are checked..." The receiving of forms is not an activity but event. Could still be intermediate catch event "6. Forms returned". That's okay.

Similarly "10. Receive updated forms" as catch event.

But element names: only tasks need step number requirement? It says every element name starts with step number. So all elements, including events, need number? Actually rule K01: steps requires every element name to start with the step number of a process description (K01). So all elements should start with step number, except plain end events and start events inside sub-process may have no number. So we need to prefix events with numbers too, except end events maybe? End events can have no number, but better to give number to all except final ends?

We'll give start event no number. End events maybe "12. Process end". But maybe allowed.
